### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d61c583baf9c4c2552c3a03d008ce0129dd0c66e` — the merge of head `c161470d5cb91860912eeb08559bafc4ebdf7ed4` into base `9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d61c583baf9c4c2552c3a03d008ce0129dd0c66e && git checkout d61c583baf9c4c2552c3a03d008ce0129dd0c66e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff c161470d5cb91860912eeb08559bafc4ebdf7ed4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff && git merge --no-ff c161470d5cb91860912eeb08559bafc4ebdf7ed4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9f736f2e2469d159422fb2ce1456bd932278ffff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review: changes needed (one should-fix, evidence only)

Head: `c161470d5cb91860912eeb08559bafc4ebdf7ed4` · reviewer review#2 (`session_016WV4czuuneAppDnJbrNejw`) · area A5 · Fixes #33050

`Clause-②: no` is right for the intended case: no authorable key, value or type moves, and an upgrade now serves what the new body ships.

Checked and fine:
- Slot tracking: `registerItem` records `type\0storageKey` only when the open body's `packageId` matches. Package items live under the composite `pkg:name` key and environment overlays under the bare key, so an overlay is never in `previous` and is never withdrawn (pinned). Items registered under the id outside a body are not recorded either (pinned).
- Withdrawal runs only after `register()` returns and only when a previous body record exists. A first registration withdraws nothing, and `uninstallPackage` forgets the record.
- Claims: bare-name and security-catalog claims the new manifest does not declare are released; `function` claims stay with the hook binder.
- Refusal: `noteItemOrder` snapshots the type's map before the first removal, and the `packageBody` record is noted, so a later refusal in the same run restores items, claims, the record and the original order (pinned).
- CI: 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed; mergeable clean.

**should-fix (evidence, likely no code change):** the change has a wider reach than install-local. Any second `registerApp` under the same id now withdraws what the first body wrote and the second does not. That is right for an upgrade, but it would also remove items if some code path registers one id twice with different bodies (a plugin contributing in two calls, a legacy `app.*` service plus a manifest, a boot-time re-register). I found one same-id pair, `com.objectstack.metadata-objects` (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` and `packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts`). Both are objects-only and identical, so it is unaffected. I could not rule out others statically. Please boot a stock showcase (or CRM) on this head and confirm it logs no `[Registry] Withdrew` line, then paste the count in the PR body. If a line appears at boot, that caller needs its own fix before this lands.

Out of scope as the body says (objects, object extensions, picklist extensions): fine for this card.

The withdrawal line goes through the same `this.log` channel as the other `[Registry]` lines, so the debug stream that shows those 653 would also show a withdrawal. No boot-time caller registers one id twice with different bodies on the showcase stack.
- `Clause-②: no` stands, as in the previous review.
